chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurarah, who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): A man had two hundred dirhams, excluding one dirham, for eleven months. Then he acquired one dirham after that in the twelfth month, so two hundred dirhams became complete with him. Is there zakat upon it? He said: 'No, until the year (hawl) passes over it while it is two hundred dirhams. If it was one hundred and fifty dirhams, and he acquired fifty after a month had passed, there is no zakat upon him until the year passes over the two hundred.'

I said to him: If he had two hundred dirhams, excluding one dirham, and days passed over them before the month ended, then he acquired one dirham, and a year passed over the dirhams along with that one dirham, is there zakat upon it? He said: 'Yes. If the year did not pass over all of them together, there is nothing upon him regarding it.'
Zurarah and Muhammad ibn Muslim said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Whichever man has wealth and the year passes over it, he must pay its zakat.'
I said to him: If he gifted it before its due date by a month or two days? He said: 'There is nothing upon him ever.'

And Zurarah narrated from him that he said: 'This is like a man who broke his fast for one day during his residence in the month of Ramadan, then he leaves at the end of the day on a journey, and he intends by that journey to invalidate the expiation that became obligatory upon him.'

He said: 'When he saw the twelfth new moon, zakat became obligatory upon him. But if he had gifted it before that, it would be valid and there would be nothing upon him. This is like the one who left (on journey) then broke his fast. He does not prevent what has become obligatory upon him. As for what has not become obligatory upon him, he has the right to prevent it. And it is permissible for him to prevent the wealth of others regarding what has become obligatory upon them.'

Zurarah said: I said to him: A man had two hundred dirhams and he gifted them to one of his brothers, or his children, or his family, to flee from the zakat, and he did that before its due date by a month. He said: 'When the twelfth month enters, the year has passed over it and zakat has become obligatory upon him regarding it.'

I said to him: If he made a new gift (or altered the status) regarding it before the year? He said: 'That is valid for him.' I said: He fled from the zakat with it. He said: 'He did not bring upon himself anything greater than what he prevented from its zakat.'

I said to him: He has the power to reclaim it. He said: 'What does it matter to me if he has the power to reclaim it, and it has already left his ownership?' I said: He gave it to him on a condition. He said: 'If he named it a gift, the gift is valid, the condition falls away, and he guarantees the zakat.'

I said to him: How does the condition fall away, the gift remain valid, and he guarantee the zakat? He said: 'This is a flawed condition, the guaranteed gift is valid, and the zakat is binding upon him as a punishment for him.'
Then he said: 'That is for him if he bought a house, or land, or fields with it.'

Then Zurarah said: I said to him: Indeed your father said to me: 'Whoever flees it from the zakat, he must pay it.' He said: 'My father is truthful (peace be upon him). He must pay it for what was obligatory upon him, and for what was not obligatory upon him, there is nothing upon him regarding it.'

Then he said: 'What do you think if a man was unconscious for a day then died, and his prayer was lost, would he have to pay it after he died?' I said: No, unless he had regained consciousness from his day. Then he said: 'If a man fell ill in the month of Ramadan then died in it, would he be required to fast on his behalf?' I said: No. He said: 'So too the man does not pay regarding his wealth except what the year has passed over.'

The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And so there is no zakat on produce until it reaches the limit upon which zakat becomes obligatory, after harvesting, threshing, and deducting its consumption and the ruler's tax.
ai.seo_question: When does the obligation of zakat begin on silver wealth if it is acquired gradually?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated by Zurara from Imam al-Baqir and Imam al-Sadiq, establishes the principle of 'hawl' (lunar year) as the critical threshold for zakat liability on silver, emphasizing that the obligation attaches only when the full amount remains in possession for a complete year. It further elucidates the legal nuance of 'farr' (avoidance) by comparing the timing of wealth transfer to fasting in Ramadan, ruling that gifts made before the hawl completes are valid and exempt the owner, whereas those made after the liability has triggered do not absolve the original owner. The text also clarifies that partial accumulation or conditional gifts do not negate the obligation if the hawl has already passed over the nisab.
